Admission ties a seat to one amateur station on the national callsign register. The applicant gives a callsign and licensed address; the node reads the regulator's database, rejects a used address, then asks for three signed QSL cards from three continents. Cards arrive by mail over months.

Fifty clones need fifty licenses and fifty antenna sites: 90 dollars fee, 700 transceiver, 400 antenna, 60 mast, near 62,500 dollars before one card returns. A tundra shack and a wharf rig hold separate callsigns, and an anchor counts by its harbour, not the water every hull floats in.
